content.rationale: the page composition of the viewer: media/webview.html serves the panel regions the page interface names and links the four stylesheets the composed page uses, including styles/search.css, so the search field and its match marks are styled by the module that owns them; src/webview/main.ts is the composition root that receives the graph across the webview seam, builds and orders it, and attaches the renderer, the interaction state, the keyboard equivalents, the presentation, the fit action, the detail panel and find-by-text search to those regions. The renderer's drawing and the interaction's viewport transform are mounted on the one surface the page interface declares (ympqvvwr): the composition hands the renderer the two drawing layers that surface holds and hands the interaction the surface itself as the element its pan and zoom are written to, so the viewport the interaction writes and the graph the renderer draws share a single coordinate space. What that space is stays the two modules' — the origin the renderer subtracts is rtlotqvy's and the mapping from the canvas to the layout through it is noplrntp's — and the composition decides only which element carries both. The search is attached exactly once, after the interaction controller exists, with the canvas, the controller the page interface declares, the current graph and its labels. What the composition hands it is that interface's whole controller (ympqvvwr): the queue the composition routes user input through (ywullzun), whose reads pass straight to the interaction, plus the centring member the interface declares forwarded to the interaction controller through that same queue, so an ask the search makes is held beside the selection it comes with and runs after it in the order the search made them. Every later graph is a revision swap: the interaction state keeps the selection, pan and zoom, the detail panel re-renders the selected node, and the search is handed the new graph and labels, so the active query re-marks the reloaded graph and the same field keeps its value instead of a second controller being attached. The standard page lifecycle notifications (pagehide, beforeunload, unload) dispose the search, so no field, listener or match mark outlives the page. The detail panel's four relationship sections list each id in its place as the entry the id is: an id the graph has a node for is listed as an activatable control, and a pointer click or Enter or Space while that entry has the focus runs the same selection a click on the node's own box runs, so the selection moves and the panel re-renders the named node's detail, while an id whose other edge end names no node document stays listed as the plain id and is inert, selecting nothing, leaving the detail as it was and reporting no error. That activation also asks the interaction to centre the viewport on the node it selects (wzsxvmvw): the composition makes the request on the composed interaction controller's own centring member of the page interface (ympqvvwr), naming the id the activation selected, and the move itself — the pan, the limits that bind it per axis and the zoom it leaves alone — is the interaction's (noplrntp), where an activation's centring is the rule's second trigger beside the focus arrival it already answers. The composition therefore decides where the ask sits and which node it names, and neither how far the view moves nor which axis holds it: what an activation is and which node it selects stay kwxutvpw's, so no second account of either is written here. The request changes nothing else the activation does — the selection and the detail region are exactly what they were — and an id whose edge names no node document asks for nothing at all, so the viewport stays exactly where it was (rusopkql). Nor is any other event of the page an ask the composition makes: a click on a node's own box selects and moves nothing of the viewport, the search's field opening and the query typed into it select nothing of the viewport's and move nothing, the keyboard equivalents reach focus through the interaction's own rule, and a ref path's activation opens a file and moves nothing (rptlovpt). The search's key presses are the one further trigger the centring move takes on the composed page, and the ask they carry is the module's, not this composition's (uowtmmqw): where Enter or Shift+Enter in the field selects a node, it is the search module that asks the interaction for the centring move on the node its selection lands on (uryrrttr), made on the controller the page interface declares (ympqvvwr) — the one this composition mounts the module with, whose centring member it forwards to the interaction controller through the input queue (ywullzun). The composition composes and forwards: it neither makes that ask nor adds one beside it, initiates no centring request of its own on the opening, the typing or the key press, and decides neither which node the walk selects (yqwsztww) nor how far the move goes or what holds it — the move started that way is the interaction's (noplrntp, wzsxvmvw) — while a key press that selects nothing asks for nothing, so the viewport stays where it was (uowtmmqw). The composition's own ask inventory therefore stays the activation's: the detail panel's activation of a listed id remains the one centring request the page makes itself (wzsxvmvw, kwxutvpw), and the search's is the module's, carried through the interface the composition hands it. Each listed id is marked, on the element that holds that id and no other, with the recorded vocabulary of two class names (sqwusxql): an id the graph has a node document for carries detail__entry, and an id that names none carries detail__entry--inert as its whole class. Exactly one of the two is on any listed entry — never neither and never both, and never on a container holding more than one id — so the markup is always readable as the answer to which case the entry is, and the class follows the id's own case rather than the section it is listed in. The panel authors no appearance beyond that mark: it declares no style rule, no colour, no cursor and no hover or focus treatment, and the look of a listed id is carried through these two names by the stylesheet rules written against them, as the appearance decisions settle it (mwwxxzyk, tvoouwkn, rqrlnzny, qnmuwwvw, vvzptxmz, mplxzxnm, kpkstnps) and as the composition states it here without restating or narrowing any of those commitments. A second mark sits beside that pair, on a different entry and for a different case: a node whose content.ref is a list of repo-relative paths shows that value in the Content section's monospaced block with the content type on the line above and each path, in the order the list gives them, as an entry of its own — the element that holds that path and nothing else, whose whole class is detail__ref (ppkkmxxu) — so no listed-entry name reaches a path and the markup and the stylesheet meet on that one name, exactly as they meet on the two above. The block keeps the whole value, the type and every path, so the panel and the node's ref list cannot disagree about which files the body lives in, and the entries add no text, no label and no order of their own. The panel declares no appearance for that name either: the entry reads as the visible link squvoxyr commits it to through the rules the stylesheet writes against the name, and the panel fixes only the name those rules select. Each such entry is a control the keyboard can reach, and activating it — a pointer click, or Enter or Space while it has the focus — posts the page's request for that repo-relative path to be opened in the editor as one message of the page's own seam, { type: "openRef", path }, beside the node-open request the double-click already posts (rptlovpt, trxzsqpv). The request names the path and nothing else: the page does not select a node, does not change the detail region and does not move the viewport on a ref path's activation, it resolves no path and opens nothing itself — the host owns how the path is found and opened, as it owns the node document the double-click asks for — and a ref path's activation stays the Content section's own, neither re-triggering the double-click nor reaching the listed ids' activation (kwxutvpw). A value whose ref is inline shows no path and so offers nothing to activate here, and the paths themselves stay what qwzwpxws presents, in the order it presents them. The composition owns only the page shell and the entry point: the renderer, interaction, keyboard, presentation, detail and search modules keep their own behaviour.
